description: We are a team of astronomy enthusiasts from Cassiopeia, passionate about space exploration, astrophysics, and science education. We’re looking for enthusiastic teammates with interests in coding, web development, design, storytelling, or multimedia to build an engaging project together.
summary:
Ghosts of the Cosmos: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive digital storytelling project that explores the legacy of NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through a visual archive of historical machines—including the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Opportunity, InSight, and Ingenuity—our website brings these silent exptorers back into the spotlight.

Visitors can explore artifact stories, view mission photographs, follow a chronological timeline, compare planned mission lifetimes with actual achievements, and test their knowledge through interactive quizzes. Each machine also shares a crealive first-person account inspired by its real mission history.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming the history of abandoned space equipment into an accessible and engaging educational experience. It highlights that these machines are not merely forgotten hardware: they are lasting records of human curiosity, scientific discovery, and exploration beyond Earth
details:
Ghosts of the Cosmos: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

What does the project do and how does it work?

Ghosts of the Cosmos is an interactive educational storytelling website that explores NASA's robotic equipment and mission hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. It transforms historical mission information into an engaging digital archive where visitors can discover the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments.

Users can explore individual machines through interactive cards, read their mission logs and interesting facts, browse historical photographs, and follow a chronological timeline. The website also includes interactive quizzes and visual comparisons between planned mission lifetimes and actual achievements. Visitors can filter the archive by the Moon or Mars. Each featured machine has a creative first-person narrative inspired by its real mission history, making the experience more personal and memorable.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

The project makes space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and understandable, particularly for students and people interested in astronomy and science. It encourages curiosity about planetary exploration while highlighting the scientific contributions of machines whose missions have ended. Our intended impact is to preserve public awareness of these historical missions, promote interest in space science, and demonstrate that even equipment left behind can have an important scientific and historical legacy.

Tools and technologies used

We developed the website using HTML for structure, CSS for visual design and responsive layouts, and JavaScript for interactive features and functionality. Google Fonts were used for typography, while mission photographs were sourced from NASA, JPL-Caltech, and Wikimedia Commons. The website is hosted publicly on Netlify. No physical hardware was required.

What makes the project creative?

Our central creative approach is to let the machines tell their own stories. Through fictional first-person narratives based on real mission events, visitors can imagine the experiences of these silent explorers. We combined storytelling with historical facts, photographs, interactive timelines, quizzes, and mission-duration comparisons to create an experience that is both educational and emotionally engaging.

Factors considered during development

We considered historical accuracy, educational value, accessibility, usability, and visual storytelling. We used NASA, JPL, and NSSDCA mission resources as factual references and clearly distinguished creative machine narratives from historical facts. We also included text-size and reduced-motion controls to make the website more accessible. Our goal was to create a simple, engaging experience that works as an educational resource while respecting the scientific history behind every featured machine.

Project website: https://ghosts-of-cosmos.netlify.app/
